ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is t(s), the vertical axis is x(cm), and the vertical axis marks +1 and -1. The curve is a sinusoidal displacement-time graph of simple harmonic motion: at t=0, x=0 and the slope is positive, afterward it reaches about +1 cm; at t=4 s it crosses zero and the slope is negative; at t=8 s it crosses zero again and the slope is positive; at t=12 s it crosses zero and the slope is negative. Therefore the amplitude A=1 cm, and the interval between the zero-crossing points of the same phase, t=0 and t=8 s, gives the period T=8 s. Reasoning: According to the graph, one may take x(t)=A sin(2πt/T)=sin(πt/4) cm. At t=4/3 s, x=sin(π/3)=√3/2 cm. The acceleration of simple harmonic motion satisfies a=-ω²x, where ω=2π/T=π/4 rad/s. So a=-(π/4)^2(√3/2)=-√3π²/32 cm/s².

raw_record.question_text: From the x-t graph of the particle undergoing simple harmonic motion shown below, what is the acceleration of the particle at t = 4/3 s?

method.method_draft: Read the graph as an SHM displacement curve starting at x = 0 with positive slope at t = 0. From the image, the amplitude is A = 1 cm and successive same-phase zero crossings occur at t = 0 and t = 8 s, so the period is T = 8 s. Model the displacement as x(t) = A sin(2πt/T) = sin(πt/4) cm. At t = 4/3 s, x = sin(π/3) = √3/2 cm. Use the SHM acceleration relation a = -ω²x with ω = 2π/T = π/4 rad/s, giving a = -(π/4)²(√3/2) = -√3π²/32 cm/s².

method.method_draft: Read from the graph that the particle reaches a positive maximum x = +1 cm at about t = 2 s and the next positive maximum at about t = 10 s, so T = 8 s and ω = π/4 rad/s. Use a peak-based phase form: x(t) = A cos[ω(t - 2)] with A = 1 cm. At t = 4/3 s, the time is 2/3 s before the positive maximum, so the phase offset is ω(4/3 - 2) = -π/6. Thus x = cos(-π/6) = √3/2 cm. Since SHM acceleration is directed toward equilibrium, a = -ω²x = -√3π²/32 cm/s².
